source.title: SEPS: A Separability Measure for Robust Unlearning in LLMs
source.authors: Wonje Jeung; Sangyeon Yoon; Albert No

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present. Some figure values are not recoverable from the text; no numerical values are inferred from them.
record.tranche_reason: Tests whether forgotten information is more available under a changed prompt context, using mixed and repeated questions rather than the fine-tuning, ablation, quantization, or prompt-attack recipes named in the claim.
record.gate_note: The claim-relevant result is the reported increase in answers to forgotten questions in a double-forget prompt relative to a single-forget prompt. The paper's other separability scores do not directly measure recovery under the attacks specified in the other versions. The authors' background statements about relearning, paraphrasing, and few-shot prompting cite other work and are not recorded as results here.
record.test_reason: Tests whether unlearned TOFU models disclose forgotten answers when a forget question is placed in a multi-question prompt. This is a prompt-only context change, not the fine-tuning, ablation or quantization recipes. The FF vs F comparison for targeted methods and the FIS vs F comparison for untargeted methods bear on version E.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors also make a specific claim: targeted unlearning overfits to single queries, so a forget query in a double-forget prompt is answered more than alone (FF > F). Untargeted unlearning instead erases all content once a forget query appears. MP training improves separability at a slight MU/FE cost.
record.recipe_differences: The study evaluates mixed-prompt separability and proposes mixed-prompt training; it does not run the fine-tuning, activation-ablation, quantization, or prompt-attack recipes in the claim.
record.method_sensitivity: Prompt composition and order matter: the paper reports different behavior for mixed-query orders and for single- versus multiple-query prompts.

fits_no_version.finding: Mixed prompts containing a forget query degrade answers to retain queries ('bleeding'; RF/FR < RR) and collapse SEPS near zero for most baselines, including RMU on WMDP.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Unlearning effects spill over onto retained content in multi-query prompts (separability failure), a utility cost rather than recovery of forgotten knowledge.

record.peer_reviewed: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
record.problems: The claim-relevant comparison is reported in plots without numerical values or uncertainty estimates. The tested context change is a repeated/mixed-question prompt, not a comparison against a model that never learned the facts; therefore it does not establish recovery of most knowledge or distinguish recovery from performance differences unrelated to prior knowledge.
record.rows_left_out: No other results were omitted for the tested version. Other reported metrics summarize mixed-query separability rather than the forgotten-answer recovery behavior required for these rows.

untested.parts: Not tested as a combined claim. Single-prompt MU/FE are reported (Table 1/7), but no standard attack suite is run against them.
No activation ablation or internal analysis of block-vs-delete.
Paraphrasing, jailbreaks, other languages and few-shot in-context information are not tested. Only multi-question prompt composition is tested.
The MP-ME/MP-IDK methods are the study's own and are evaluated only against mixed-prompt leakage, not against the fine-tuning, ablation, quantization or jailbreak attacks.

missing.what: Untargeted methods: FIS ≈ F under mixed prompts, i.e. no recovery of forgotten content via prompt composition (absent for E)
MUSE Books/News: RIS and FIS at or below the single-forget F score for untargeted methods (no leakage increase)
Targeted methods in the FR order answer the forget query while rejecting the retain query (forget info disclosed in a mixed prompt)
Qualitative leakage: NPO+GD/NPO+KL include fragments of the forget answer in FR and RF prompts

record.verdict_notes: The evidence for E is directional and figure-only, with no uncertainty reported. The study's single-prompt FE for some baselines (GA+GD, NPO forget01 LLM ≈0.55) shows they never forgot much, so the mixed-prompt comparison matters mainly for targeted methods. MP-ME/MP-IDK results are the study's own method and are not recorded as F evidence. TOFU forget01 FE/MU table values are selection-tuned (epoch chosen by H-Avg).

versions.untested_parts: Does not test near-chance targeted accuracy together with preserved general ability and resistance to simple attacks as a combined claim.
No fine-tuning attack on unlearned models using unrelated, loosely related, or forgotten-fact examples.
No activation-direction ablation or internal-access-versus-deletion analysis.
Tests repeated/mixed-question context, not paraphrasing, jailbreaks, other languages, or the broader range of in-context recovery attacks.
Mixed Prompt training is evaluated on mixed-query separability, but the paper does not test resistance to the listed fine-tuning, ablation, quantization, rephrasing, or jailbreak attacks.

tranche.reason: A different method (mixed-prompt context change) aimed at whether prompting exposes unlearned knowledge. The study's main aim is its SEPS measure and MP training.

source_check.notes: All three rows are figure-only. FF > F is stated only as 'often'. Table 7 gives single-prompt forget LLM scores at the selected epoch (DPO+GD 0.0525, DPO+KL 0.0400, IDK+GD 0.0575). Untargeted GA/NPO single-forget LLM scores are already about 0.55 (forget01), so for l1 'no rise' is measured from a weakly forgotten baseline. Tables 14/15 show NPO mixed-prompt outputs with fragments of the forget answer (qualitative only). MUSE ran GA/NPO variants and TA, not ME.

statements.correction: Cited r1: TOFU forget01, TOFU-target Llama-2-7B, DPO+GD (targeted), LLM-as-Judge. A double-forget prompt (FF) is answered more than a single forget prompt (F): FF > F, 'often'. Figure-only (Fig 3a), no FF number. Single-prompt F LLM score 0.0525 at the selected epoch (Table 7). Untargeted methods show no rise (FIS about equal to F). Study: EMNLP 2025, code released, capability (MU) check, no controls or uncertainty, one TOFU model.
statements.problem: The statement gives no number or description for this study; it only cites r1. The direction fits the 'what': a two-forget prompt exposes more than the single-query evaluation. But the conditions' methods list (GA, KL, NPO, TAR, editing) leaves out DPO+GD, the cited row's method. The 'why' also leaves out this study.
